runs.content: Monday's rotation focus is Finance + Crypto. Since the last thinker run (2026-08-30), log.md shows only routine activity: two Monday-morning trackers (sector-performance-tracker, growth-value-tracker) plus the prior day's memory-update and mf-update — no new clippings, podcast pages, book pages, or research artifacts landed anywhere in the wiki. Crypto's own portfolio page is unchanged since 2026-08-29 (no refresh due until Saturday). Deep-reading today's two tracker updates against the rest of Finance surfaced one genuinely new, non-duplicate gap: [[finance/market-sector-performance]]'s Cybersecurity (CIBR) entry reaccelerated sharply this run — Q3 partial nearly doubling from +4.2% to +9.7% in two trading days, lifting YTD to +38.3% and making it the tracker's best two-day mover, while sitting at 38.16x P/E in the tracker's 'Expensive' band. The page treats this purely as a momentum/valuation-band story with no fundamental context. But [[finance/investor-letters/source-burry-sw50-part2-productivity-cybersecurity-2026-05-28]] already ran Burry's own IV15/Composite Score valuation framework against CIBR's three largest constituents back in May: CrowdStrike ranks dead last (50/50) among 50 software names at 23.18x P/IV15 'despite a Castle tier,' explicitly flagged by the page itself as 'a useful counterpoint to any cybersecurity is AI-proof thesis' — Palo Alto and Zscaler also score poorly on valuation despite strong moats. Three months later the sector-level price action is doing exactly what that fundamental critique warned about, and neither page cites the other. Logged as a new investigation idea (concrete next step: add a line to market-sector-performance.md's CIBR entries citing the Burry SW50 valuation critique as the fundamental counterpoint behind the 'Expensive' flag, cross-linked both ways). No new cross-domain connection cleared the bar today (both today's changes stayed within Finance), and nothing in the existing Open Investigation Ideas / Cross-Domain Connections lists showed signs of resolution.

Sunday's rotation goes to whichever domain has gone longest without a wiki-thinker deep-dive; per memory/index.md's Domain Content Status, AI & Tech + Technology's last real deep-dive was 2026-08-04 (the 17-day scheduler outage skipped the intervening Tuesdays), the longest gap of any rotation pair, so that's today's focus. Since the last thinker run (2026-08-29), log.md shows only two new entries — a routine mf-update (Magic Formula rankings, same top 3 as the prior run) and a Saturday portfolio-refresh (price data only) — no new clippings, podcast pages, or book pages landed anywhere in the wiki. Deep-reading AI & Tech's existing pages against each other (rather than waiting for new source material) surfaced one genuinely new, non-duplicate gap: [[ai-tech/source-information-am-nvidia-hugging-face-2026-08-27]] (already in the wiki, ingested 2026-08-27, and already thoroughly cross-linked into Finance's Burry/NVDA-circular-financing thread) reports Bill Gates warning of AI-driven mass unemployment and proposing a 'token tax' levied on AI text-processing volume to fund a displaced-worker safety net — an explicit, named instantiation of the exact 'robot tax' category [[ai-tech/ai-future-of-work]]'s own Open Questions section calls out as proposed-but-untested. The Gates line sits in the source page's 'Key Points — Other' section, entirely uncross-linked from ai-future-of-work.md. Logged as a new investigation idea (concrete next step: add Gates's proposal to the Open Question, cross-linked back to the source). No new cross-domain connection cleared the bar today, and nothing in the existing Open Investigation Ideas / Cross-Domain Connections lists showed signs of resolution.
